subject.title: [Feature/RFC]: Add eval-backed option discovery to avoid premature convergence in route/strategy answers

question: Should OpenClaw adopt option discovery before confident route, strategy, or choice recommendations as a default harness-neutral behavior invariant?
rationale: The issue is credible and source inspection shows the invariant is absent, but changing default recommendation behavior affects latency, tool use, prompt scope, and runtime ownership, so automation should not decide it alone.

options.title: Adopt Eval-First Default Invariant
options.body: Define the generic QA scenario and runtime-pair scope first, then add the narrow prompt/runtime contract only after the eval shape is accepted.

options.title: Keep It Opt-In
options.body: Treat the behavior as a research or best-insight profile so default turns stay lean and users explicitly choose deeper option discovery.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Decline default option discovery for now and rely on existing tool-discipline guidance plus future search-depth improvements.

recommendation.title: Adopt Eval-First Default Invariant
recommendation.body: Define the generic QA scenario and runtime-pair scope first, then add the narrow prompt/runtime contract only after the eval shape is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the strongest current routing candidate from adjacent Codex search and prompt-boundary history, though the final product call may need broader maintainer input.
